soundness_flags.label: Theorem 4 (robust-order-tightening)
soundness_flags.one_line: The order-only interval is only described as what an external LP returns, and the relative ball ranges over undefined “graph-compatible” laws; define its temporal order, exact feasible SCM/signature class, and compatibility predicate before numerical endpoint and openness claims are meaningful.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines possible parents across compatible full-time ADMGs and states that the controlled micro direct effect is identifiable by the conditional-mean adjustment formula when the outcome SCC is singleton and no bidirected edge joins the outcome to an ancestor; its positivity assumption is full observed-law support.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 119(547), pp. 1778-1795
source_verification_receipts.locator: Sections 4-5, especially the polynomial-program formulation and epsilon-sharp optimization discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article reduces discrete causal bounding under a declared causal model and assumptions to polynomial programs, and supplies anytime valid outer bounds converging to sharpness through epsilon-sharp optimization rather than exact algebraic endpoint isolation.

The paper reduces query-implied causal-order partial identification to an LP, proves tightness through witness SCMs, and reverses its signature quotient by assigning uniform mass within each equivalence cell of an unrestricted signature simplex.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract and proceedings record; primary PDF linked from the proceedings page
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The publication exists as cited and claims constraint-aware canonical-domain reduction preserving sharp LP bounds through the induced push-forward distribution; the present proposal's product-factorization distinction is not claimed to be covered by that abstract-level verification.

The paper gives a finite segment bound for applying causal identification to time-series graphs with latent confounding, depending on variables per time step and maximum direct or latent lag; it does not claim enumeration of all summary-graph refinements.
The paper derives analytical causal-effect bounds from a PAG representing a Markov-equivalence class, a different graphical-information regime from the temporal summary-graph refinement fiber.
The paper constructs confidence regions for an iid multinomial parameter with prescribed coverage and studies resulting intervals for linear functionals.
EasyRCA uses an acyclic summary causal graph, identifies adjustment sets for direct effects, and compares normal-versus-anomalous direct effects for root-cause identification.

The cited paper exists and gives quantifier elimination over real closed fields with separated combinatorial and algebraic complexity roles; its exact use for the proposed causal bit-complexity expression should be checked against the theorem statement during derivation.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define the order-only comparator as an explicit finite signature/SCM class, state its temporal partial order and constraints, and define graph compatibility as nonemptiness of the corresponding fiber before retaining the claimed rational endpoints and relative-open neighborhood.

Give the temporal-instrument witness as a compact table of the rational raw branch, its induced law, endpoint-attaining SCMs, and the two strict endpoint certificates; this converts the strictness theorem from a numerical promise into a reproducible field-level separator.

Turn the factorization-safe quotient question into a reusable criterion by first resolving the six-vertex kill test and then stating a concrete incidence-hypergraph condition with an explicit quotient-size upper bound.

recommended_next_step: Revise Theorem 4 by formally defining the order-only comparator and compatible-law neighborhood, then advance the sharp refinement-envelope and quotient-fidelity kernel to Stage 0 at field tier.
